---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/Infisical/infisical
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: infisical/infisical:v0.162.19 (plus redis:7-alpine)
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: infisical
quirks:
  - "START FROM docker-compose.prod.yml, NOT FROM EITHER COMPOSE A FILE SCAN FINDS FIRST. backend-go/docker-compose.test.yml and .github/resources/docker-compose.be-test.yml are test harnesses, and the first of them has literal sample encryption and auth keys sitting in its environment block. Copying that file is how a published sample key ends up encrypting somebody's real secrets. docker-compose.prod.yml is three services: backend, db and redis."
  - "⛔ PIN THE TAG. UPSTREAM'S OWN COMPOSE TELLS YOU TO, IN A COMMENT ON THE IMAGE LINE, AND THEN DOES NOT. Use infisical/infisical:v0.162.19, verified present on Docker Hub at 0.76 GB compressed and updated 2026-08-10, the same day as that GitHub release. The leading v IS PART OF THE TAG: the registry has no bare 0.162.19. Also DROP pull_policy: always from that service, which with a moving tag would quietly upgrade your secrets manager on every restart, and PIN THE REDIS SERVICE TOO: upstream writes a completely unversioned image name for it. redis:7-alpine is the version their own test compose uses."
  - "⛔⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR, AND WHEN: WHOEVER COMPLETES THE ONE-SHOT INSTANCE SETUP, AND UNTIL THEY DO, ANYONE CAN. On first boot the server config row is written with initialized:false and allowSignUp:true (super-admin-service.ts:203-204). The very next account created becomes the SUPER ADMIN of the instance and the owner of its first organization. THE GOOD NEWS, verified in the same file: setup is ONE-SHOT (bootstrapInstance throws \"Instance has already been set up\" at :582-584) and, because this is a self-hosted instance rather than their cloud, the same code path flips allowSignUp to FALSE when it completes (:562-565 and :694-700). So the window is real but it CLOSES PERMANENTLY the moment someone walks through it. Your job is to be that someone, during the deploy, before you hand over the URL."
  - "⛔ CLOSE IT FROM THE DEPLOY, NOT FROM A BROWSER: POST /api/v1/admin/bootstrap. admin-router.ts:801-844 exposes an UNAUTHENTICATED endpoint taking {email, password, organization} that creates the super admin and the organization in one call, and returns a machine identity with a token as well. Call it as soon as the app answers, from the deploy itself. That is the difference between a window measured in minutes and one measured in however long it takes a human to open a browser. Generate the password ALPHANUMERIC so there is nothing to escape in JSON, send the body ON STDIN and never in argv, hand both values to the user once in the session, and never write either into this file. If the call comes back \"Instance has already been set up\" and you did not do it, somebody else did: do not hand that instance over, destroy it and redeploy."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, so you can tell a leak from a normal response. GET /api/status answers without auth and is what the docs use to check the deployment is alive. GET /api/v1/admin/config also answers without auth, deliberately, but admin-router.ts:96-115 returns a REDUCED payload to a caller who is not a super admin: initialized, allowSignUp, the allowed signup domain, the enabled login methods and the password policy. That is a feature, not a leak, and it is what lets the script in the body of this file prove the instance is claimed without holding any credential. The login and signup pages are reachable, by definition. Everything that touches a secret is behind authentication."
  - "⛔⛔ ENCRYPTION_KEY IS THE ONE THAT ENDS THE STORY IF IT IS LOST, AND UPSTREAM SAYS SO IN THEIR OWN DOCS: \"Without this key, you cannot decrypt secrets even if you restore the database\" (docker-compose.mdx:506). It is OPTIONAL in the schema (env.ts:201-202), which is the trap: a deploy without it boots fine and then throws at the first operation that needs the instance root key, with \"Tried to encrypt with instance root encryption key, but no root encryption key is set\" (crypto.ts:286-293), which reads like a bug rather than a missing variable. Generate one, pass it, and pass the SAME one on every redeploy, for the life of the instance. Two forms exist and crypto.ts:295-322 shows exactly how they differ: ROOT_ENCRYPTION_KEY is used as a 256-bit key with base64 encoding and takes precedence, ENCRYPTION_KEY is used as a 128-bit key and is the one their self-host docs and .env.example use. PICK ONE, NEVER SET BOTH, AND NEVER CHANGE IT. Changing it does not rotate anything; it orphans every secret already stored."
  - "⛔⛔ SET COOKIE_SECRET_SIGN_KEY. IT HAS A DEFAULT AND THAT DEFAULT IS PUBLISHED IN THE REPOSITORY. env.ts:253-256 gives it a hardcoded fallback string, and app.ts:109-110 hands that value to @fastify/cookie as the signing secret for every cookie the app sets. It is NOT in .env.example, which is why practically nobody sets it: it is not that people ignore the instruction, it is that there is no instruction. On a private laptop that is nothing. On a public hostname, in front of a secrets manager, a cookie signing key that anyone can read on GitHub is the sharpest thing in this file. Generate at least 32 characters of your own and pass it in the deploy env."
  - "SET AUTH_SECRET, AND REUSE IT. env.ts:281 makes it required, with a legacy fallback to JWT_AUTH_SECRET for old deployments. It signs the access, refresh, signup, invite and MFA JWTs whose lifetimes are configured immediately below it, so changing it on a redeploy invalidates every session and every refresh token at once. Generate it as a long random value and keep it with the encryption key."
  - "⛔ DELETE THE BUNDLED db SERVICE AND WIRE THE MANAGED ONE, OR A REDEPLOY TAKES THE SECRETS WITH IT. docker-compose.prod.yml ships postgres:14-alpine on a local volume with credentials that come from the same .env, and it works perfectly, right up until the VM is replaced. Remove the service AND the depends_on entry naming it, then set DB_CONNECTION_URI from what redu injects. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends DATABASE_URL as a postgresql:// URL along with PGHOST, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD and PGDATABASE, and it only APPENDS to the project .env, it never edits your compose, so the compose must interpolate: DB_CONNECTION_URI: ${DATABASE_URL}. PROVE IT AFTER BOOT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because absence alone is not evidence: run `sudo docker exec <backend container> printenv DB_CONNECTION_URI` and confirm the host in it is your managed database's private IP (the positive half, which also proves your exec command ran at all), THEN run `sudo docker ps --format '{{.Image}}' | grep -c postgres` and confirm it is 0. If the first command errors, the second one's zero means nothing."
  - "ONE MANAGED POSTGRES IS ENOUGH, AND NO SUPERUSER IS NEEDED. redu's managed Postgres serves exactly ONE database, because databaseController.ts:167 creates it with the app user as OWNER and :170,177 write pg_hba entries for that database plus `postgres` only; anything else on that server is refused at authentication with SQLSTATE 28000 and superuser does not help. Infisical wants exactly one database and creates its own tables inside whatever it is given, so nothing here trips that rule. Its schema generates UUID primary keys in the database (db/utils.ts:10, knex.fn.uuid()); redu's managed Postgres defaults to major 16, where that needs no extension. Passing db_extensions: [\"pgcrypto\"] costs nothing, is applied by the DB VM as the postgres superuser at provision time, and removes the question entirely."
  - "⛔ THE DATABASE CONNECTION IS NOT ENCRYPTED UNLESS YOU GIVE IT A CA, AND THIS IS A SECRETS MANAGER. backend/src/db/instance.ts:3-8: the SSL config is FALSE unless DB_ROOT_CERT is set, and putting sslmode= in the connection URI does NOT change that on its own; the sslmode value is only consulted when a root cert is present. redu keeps the managed database on a private network that nothing else reaches, which is why every other entry in this library treats that as sufficient, but for this app say it out loud to the user rather than letting them assume TLS. If they want it, DB_ROOT_CERT takes a base64-encoded CA PEM."
  - "REDIS IS REQUIRED, NOT OPTIONAL, AND THE APP REFUSES TO START WITHOUT IT. env.ts:602-603 is a schema refine demanding REDIS_URL, REDIS_SENTINEL_HOSTS or REDIS_CLUSTER_HOSTS. Keep the in-compose redis: it is a cache and a job queue rather than a system of record, so losing it costs a queue drain and not data, and it keeps a second managed datastore off the bill. Three things to fix in upstream's version of that service: PIN it (they write a bare image name), keep its volume so queued work survives a restart, and NEVER publish 6379. It has no password: [REDACTED:value] ALLOW_EMPTY_PASSWORD line in their compose is a Bitnami-image variable and does nothing at all on the official redis image, so what actually protects that Redis is that it is only reachable on the compose network. If you ever move it to a managed Redis instead, redu appends REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT and REDIS_URL to the project .env and Infisical reads REDIS_URL directly, so nothing needs rewriting."
  - "SET SITE_URL TO THE PUBLIC HTTPS URL, WHICH MEANS GENERATING THE HOSTNAME UP FRONT. .env.example ships it as a localhost value and env.ts:258-259 only strips a trailing slash from whatever you give it. It is used to build the links in invite and password-reset emails and to anchor the browser origin, so a wrong value produces mail nobody can click and login flows that look broken rather than misconfigured. Generate the dname yourself in the full `infisical-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud` form and pass it to deploy_compose as dname so SITE_URL can be set in the same call; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match."
  - "TURN THE OUTBOUND CALLS OFF, DELIBERATELY, AND TELL THE USER YOU DID. TELEMETRY_ENABLED is set to true INSIDE THE IMAGE (Dockerfile.standalone-infisical), so leaving it out of your .env does not disable it, you have to set TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false explicitly. env.ts:261-263 also carries a default PostHog host and project key, and ANNOUNCEMENTS_ENABLED defaults to true, which is an outbound Contentful fetch. None of it ships secret material, and turning it off is still the right default for a self-hosted, EU-hosted secrets platform. Say which ones you turned off in the handover rather than doing it silently."
  - "PORT 8080, AND CHANGE UPSTREAM'S MAPPING. The image sets PORT 8080 and EXPOSEs it (Dockerfile.standalone-infisical); their compose publishes it on host port 80, which on redu is an unnecessary collision with nothing to gain. Map 8080:8080 and pass port 8080 to deploy_compose. redu terminates TLS in front of it and the image already ships HTTPS_ENABLED false, so the app never tries to serve TLS itself. Health probe: GET /api/status, which is the check upstream's own docs use."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED. standalone-entrypoint.sh is three lines and simply execs the app, which runs its own migrations in-process at boot; upstream's upgrade instructions tell you to watch the backend log for migration messages rather than to run anything. The container also runs as USER 1001, a non-root uid, which is why nothing here needs a privileged mount."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE, AND THE ONLY NUMBER UPSTREAM PUBLISHES IS THE IMAGE'S OWN HEAP CAP.
